title: Search a 2D Matrix
description:
# Search a 2D Matrix

You are given an `m x n` integer matrix `matrix` with two ordering rules:

* Each row is sorted in non-decreasing order.
* The first integer of each row is greater than the last integer of the previous row.

Given an integer `target`, return `true` if `target` appears in `matrix`; otherwise return `false`.

The required time complexity is `O(log(m * n))`.

## Example 1

**Input:** matrix = [[1,3,5,7],[10,11,16,20],[23,30,34,60]], target = 3

**Output:** true

## Example 2

**Input:** matrix = [[1,3,5,7],[10,11,16,20],[23,30,34,60]], target = 13

**Output:** false

## Constraints

* `m == matrix.length`
* `n == matrix[i].length`
* `1 <= m, n <= 100`
* `-10000 <= matrix[i][j], target <= 10000`

tests.description: Target found in the first row
Target absent between two matrix values
Target at the first value of a later row
Target at the last value of a middle row
Target smaller than the first value
Target larger than the last value
Negative target at a row boundary

solutions.name: Flattened Closed-Interval Binary Search
solutions.description:
## Approach

Treat the matrix as a virtual sorted array of length `m * n` in row-major order. Run a standard closed-interval binary search over virtual indices and map each index back to a cell with division and modulo.

## Key Insight

For a matrix with `n` columns, virtual index `mid` corresponds to `matrix[mid / n][mid % n]`. The row-order rule makes this virtual array sorted, so ordinary binary search is valid.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(log(m*n))
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Flattened Lower Bound Then Check
solutions.description:
## Approach

Find the first virtual index whose matrix value is greater than or equal to `target`. After the loop, check whether that candidate index is inside the matrix and exactly equals `target`.

## Key Insight

This is the same lower-bound pattern from one-dimensional binary search. Only the value lookup changes: every comparison maps the virtual index back into `(row, column)`.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(log(m*n))
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Row Selection Then Column Binary Search
solutions.description:
## Approach

First binary search the last row whose first value is not greater than `target`; this is the only possible row. Then run a normal binary search inside that row.

## Key Insight

The row starts form a sorted list of row ranges. Once the possible row is selected, the problem reduces to ordinary one-dimensional binary search inside that row.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(log m + log n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Recursive Virtual Binary Search
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use recursion over the virtual flattened index range. Each recursive call checks the middle virtual index, maps it to a matrix cell, and recurses into the only half that may still contain the target.

## Key Insight

The recursive form makes the divide-and-conquer structure explicit while preserving the same row-major index mapping as iterative flattened binary search.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(log(m*n))
- Space Complexity: O(log(m*n))
